item.title: Nvidia controversy: Trump unlikely to raise Alice Huang allegations with Xi Jinping
item.description: Next week, US President Donald Trump will engage with Chinese President Xi Jinping at the APEC summit, despite claims regarding businesswoman Alice Huang and her connection to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang surfacing in the media. Sources reveal that Trump won't cover these allegations during his talks with Xi. Nvidia is conducting a separate inquiry into Alice Huang's supposed espionage, which Beijing firmly denies amid the ongoing investigation.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: US flight disruption: Air India flags possible delays to US-bound services
item.description: Travelers on Air India flights faced significant delays due to a nationwide communication failure that affected the FAA, leading to a temporary ground halt of all flight departures across the U.S. Although the ground stop has since been lifted, passengers should brace for ongoing disruptions as the situation unfolds. Investigations are in progress to pinpoint the cause behind this communication breakdown, with safety being the top priority for FAA officials.
item.dc:creator: Shivanghi Payal

item.title: US flight chaos: Thousands stranded as FAA halts take-offs nationwide – what we know so far
item.description: A nationwide ground stop for flights in the United States was ordered due to a telecommunications outage. The Federal Aviation Administration implemented the measure to ensure safety as communications were disrupted. Thousands of passengers faced delays and cancellations across various airports. Investigations are ongoing to determine the cause of the telecommunications failure, but no security threat has been identified.

item.title: 95-year-old Houston man finally gets birth certificate after decades-long search
item.description: James Dorsey, a 95-year-old resident of Houston, has finally secured his long-missing birth certificate, a significant milestone that eluded him for decades. Born on a Louisiana plantation, Dorsey discovered the absence of this key document while planning his marriage. With the assistance of attorney Raynique Keelen, necessary corrections were made to his birth record, affirming his status as a recognized American citizen.

item.title: Texas appeals court says HOA isn't liable for fight between resident and volunteer treasurer
item.description: In a pivotal ruling, a Texas appeals court declared that the Lake Bonanza Property Owners Association bears no responsibility for a brawl involving its volunteer treasurer. This incident unfolded during a budget meeting where tensions escalated, leading to a physical confrontation between treasurer Courtney and a resident after the meeting was recorded. The court determined that Courtney acted outside his official capacity, resulting in a decision favoring the homeowners association.

item.title: Texas brothers convicted in $240 million cattle investment fraud targeting 2,200 investors
item.description: Convicted of a fraudulent cattle investment scheme, Joshua and Jason Link swindled over 2,200 investors, misleading them into thinking their money was turning into cattle purchases. Their actions resulted in colossal financial damages, as they raised more than $240 million through non-existent contracts. Investigations uncovered that funds were misused for personal luxuries rather than fulfilling their financial promises to investors.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Rob Roy MacGregor’s gravestone;scans suggest first carvings were made 1,000years before he died
item.description: A recent study has uncovered that the gravestone of Rob Roy MacGregor, found at Balquhidder Parish Church, has roots that stretch back an astonishing thousand years prior to his life. Utilizing 3D imaging techniques, researchers have discovered that the stone features carvings from multiple eras, hinting at a potential connection to early medieval Christianity through its intricate designs. For those intrigued, digital models have been made publicly accessible for exploration.

item.title: Missouri appeals court upholds $800,000 award in delivery van crash case
item.description: A Missouri appeals court upheld an $800,000 jury verdict in favor of Amy Bolandis following a traffic accident. It was determined that the delivery van driver failed to check for oncoming vehicles before merging into Bolandis's lane, leading to the collision. The court ruled decisively that Bolandis was not speeding, emphasizing the responsibility of all drivers to prioritize safety when entering traffic.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A 13-inch sculpture model that Barbara Hepworth gave her doctor has resurfaced for auction in Cornwall, where the aluminium-and-string study for her famous Winged Figure could fetch as much as £80,000
item.description: Barbara Hepworth's miniature sculpture of Winged Figure, a personal gift to Dr. Roger Slack, is returning to auction. This 13-inch artwork could reach an estimated value of £80,000 at the auction in Cornwall. Roger Slack's relationship with Hepworth grew out of their doctor-patient dynamic within the arts community in St Ives. The sculpture reflects Hepworth's artistic legacy and her significant public work on Oxford Street.

item.title: Ohio Appeals Court revives inmate's challenge to foreclosure over improper service claims
item.description: A foreclosure dispute surrounding Mamadou Diallo is back in court due to notification concerns. The Ohio appeals court has ruled that Diallo's subsequent actions do not establish proof of proper service for the foreclosure notice. Having been convicted for the murder of his spouse, Diallo contested the foreclosure judgment on the grounds of claimed service deficiencies.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Teens raised by strict, obey-without-question parents tend to hold more antisocial beliefs, a US study found, and they also showed small rises in anxiety and depression
item.description: Authoritarian parenting can lead to persistent antisocial thoughts among teenagers, affecting their social behavior and emotional well-being. Research indicates that strict parenting fosters beliefs that may justify rule-breaking and aggression. While not all adolescents display increased anxiety or depression, some experience heightened symptoms over time. These findings suggest that parenting styles significantly impact adolescent development and understanding of social norms.
